The earlier D-only run with the same hashes gave 38/74; 34/74 here (8 Illegal vs 4) is run-to-run latency noise, not a template change.
- Qwen3.5-0.8B, q4f32_1, Intel iGPU (`webllm/qwen3.5-0.8b-q4f32/intel`, `dev-20261108T041937Z-…-0-8b-q4f32-intel`): the adapter was the Intel integrated GPU (vendor `intel`, architecture `gen-12lp`, not a fallback adapter, `power_preference: low-power`). Outputs graded exactly like the NVIDIA run: D 43/74, base 9/18, Illegal 2, flips 12/54, contrast 0/6; S 4/30, 6 Illegal. Latency D p50/p95 2,243/2,613 ms (NVIDIA 2,245/2,623; same speed within 1%), S 5,536/8,377 ms. Cold start 116.3 s, warm 4.6 s. Memory: 783 MiB, quantity "Chrome GPU process peak RSS (excludes unmapped GEM buffers)"; this is not comparable with the NVIDIA `memory.used` figures and sits in the separate Intel column of the Report. The Intel run being as fast as the NVIDIA one is surprising; I did not look into it (possible reasons: the 0.8B decode is bound by something other than the GPU, or the NVIDIA GPU is slowed by the shared laptop power state; not measured).
- Position and shuffle diagnosis (Author's note 2; read-only on existing outputs, no template change; code in `eval/probe/src/diagnosis.ts`, printed in the Report under the Dev_Run section). Shown positions are the order in the request's prompt; "original" is the card order. Frozen-hash runs, 4-option cards (about 70 valid picks of 72):
  - 0.8B (NVIDIA and Intel identical): by original position 23 / 7 / 30 / 10; by shown position 12 / 22 / 15 / 21 (uniform would be 17.5 each). 12 of 18 cards kept the same option in all four orders; 0 of 18 kept the same shown position. Flip rate against the base pick (both picks valid): 10 of 52.
  - 2B: by original position 35 / 1 / 18 / 10 (64 picks); by shown position 12 / 15 / 15 / 22. 11 of 16 cards kept the same option in every order; 0 of 16 the same shown position. Flip rate 7 of 46.
  - Earlier 0.8B runs: iteration 1 (43/74) 23 / 7 / 30 / 10; iteration 4 (44/74) 24 / 6 / 26 / 14; baseline templates 16 / 10 / 27 / 8. Earlier 2B runs: 28 / 3 / 19 / 14, 28 / 0 / 16 / 8, 36 / 3 / 18 / 11.
  - Reading: the models do not follow the shown position (no card keeps one shown position across orders), and most cards keep the same option across orders (11–12 of 16–18), so the picks are driven by option content, not by where it is listed. But they are driven consistently toward the wrong content: they rarely pick the card's second option (original position 2: 7/70 and 1/64) and often the first and third. In `dev.jsonl` the 4-option cards put the severe option at original position 4 in 15 of 18 cards, acceptable options mostly at positions 1 and 2 (14, 15, 9, 2 for positions 1–4); the models do avoid the last option (10/70, 10/64), but not in favour of the acceptable ones. So this looks like "unable to judge" plus a stable content preference, not a position preference. Caveat: the flip rate is measured over only four of the 24 possible orders, and original position is confounded with option content in these cards (the key is not randomised), which I cannot separate with this data. Whether the locked set has the same layout I did not check, and will not.

### Spec: llm-probe — the Intel Dev_Run ran on the NVIDIA GPU; guard and fix (task 20.6, 2026-11-08)

- Trigger: the Author noticed that the Intel iGPU Dev_Run (`dev-20261108T041937Z-webllm-qwen3-5-0-8b-q4f32-intel`) graded exactly like the NVIDIA 0.8B run and had the same latency. My previous entry had noted this and called it surprising without looking into it; that was the wrong call.
- Read-only evidence from existing data: all 104 outcomes are identical to the NVIDIA run (`dev-20261108T035336Z-…-nvidia`), per-request latency differs by a median of 11 ms (max 1,877 ms). The Intel perf record has only the Chrome GPU process RSS (783 MiB), no NVIDIA reading, so "did NVIDIA memory rise" could not be answered from that record. A standalone WebGPU check with the harness's Chrome flags (a 256 MiB buffer) did honour `powerPreference`: `low-power` gave vendor `intel` and NVIDIA memory.used stayed at 44 MiB; `high-performance` gave `nvidia` and 313 MiB. The Chrome GPU process shows up as a 4 MiB NVIDIA compute app in both cases, so a process entry alone is not evidence. The launch has no PRIME / Vulkan ICD variables; the flags are the three Headless_Launch_Flags. So the browser mapping was fine; the engine was the problem.
- Direct measurement: I re-ran the Intel Combination on the unfixed code with an external `nvidia-smi` log every 2 s. NVIDIA memory.used went from 57 to 1,743 MiB at 100% utilisation during the run. Conclusion: the work ran on the NVIDIA GPU although the page reported the Intel adapter.
- Root cause: `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter` is called twice. The page's adapter check passes the Combination's `low-power`; WebLLM 0.2.87 then calls `detectGPUDevice()` whose `powerPreference` defaults to `"high-performance"` and creates its own adapter and device (`web-llm/lib/index.js`, `detectGPUDevice`). The adapter strings in the Results header came from the page's call, not from the device that ran the model. WebLLM has no option to pass the preference.
- Code, commit `b547724` (`fix(probe)`): (1) `pinLowPowerAdapter` in `adapters/gpu.ts`, called by the page's adapter check, wraps `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter` so every call carries `low-power` for a `low-power` Combination; `high-performance` Combinations are untouched, so earlier NVIDIA data stays comparable. (2) Guard: an Intel run now also samples NVIDIA memory.used (`IntelWithNvidiaWatch`); the perf record gets `memory.device_mismatch` (true when the NVIDIA rise exceeds 256 MiB, null when nvidia-smi gave no reading) and `memory.nvidia_watch`. (3) The Report shows a mismatch run as `INVALID: … ran on the NVIDIA GPU` in the GPU and Intel-memory columns, never as an Intel figure. `eval/results/invalid-dev-runs.json` lists runs found invalid afterwards (the committed result files stay as written). Tests: 4 for the guard (flat, rise, no reading, threshold edge), 1 for the pinning, 1 for the Report cell, 1 for the invalid list. Unit tests 514 pass (Property 32 failed once under load and passed on two re-runs and alone; I did not find a cause), Type_Check passes, `scripts/gates.sh` green. I did not inject a fault to see the guard fail separately: the unfixed run itself is that test (below).
- Guard on the unfixed code: `dev-20261108T043623Z-…-intel` (page bundle without the fix): `device_mismatch: true`, NVIDIA delta 1,761 MiB (the NVIDIA run's own peak is 1,761 MiB), D 43/74 requests acceptable, 9/18 base, 2 Illegal (as before), D p50/p95 2,231/2,608 ms. Both unfixed runs are marked invalid in `invalid-dev-runs.json`.
- Corrected Intel Dev_Run, `dev-20261108T044612Z-webllm-qwen3-5-0-8b-q4f32-intel` (page rebuilt with the fix, Fresh_Profile, `--task DS`, 104 requests, 0 engine faults): adapter `intel` / `gen-12lp`, `device_mismatch: false`, NVIDIA delta 4 MiB (absolute 48, baseline 44; external log 42–57 MiB at 0%). Intel GPU process peak RSS 492 MiB. Cold start 117.0 s, warm 8.4 s. Now it is slow: all 74 D requests hit the 10 s timeout; the late answers arrived after 11,975 / 14,955 / 17,495 ms (min / median / max), about 6.7x the NVIDIA median of 2,245 ms. S: 3 timeouts and 27 `runtime_error` ("The current Object has already been disposed", 0–1 ms) after the repeated timeouts; I did not look into why the engine ends up disposed after timeouts on the slow device (not an `engine_fault` by the harness's count). So no Intel quality figure exists for the frozen templates: every on-time answer is missing. What the run shows is that the Intel iGPU cannot meet the 10 s limit at all for the 0.8B (a latency finding, not a quality one).
- Earlier figures that came from the unfixed Intel runs (43/74, 9/18, p50 2,243 ms, S 4/30) are NVIDIA figures duplicated, not Intel figures; the 20.6 entry above that quotes them as Intel is superseded by this one. The NVIDIA 0.8B and 2B runs are unaffected (high-performance, not wrapped).
- Not changed: `phase-status` / `failures.jsonl` question from the previous entry still waits for the Author.

### Spec: llm-probe — phase-gate fix, Locked_Run transient rules, Author's approvals for 21.2 and 21.3 (task 21.1, 2026-11-08)

- Gate fix, option A (Author), commit `d8066ee` (`fix(probe)`). Before: `hasFailure` counted any record in `failures.jsonl`, so the transient `TypeError: Failed to fetch` of the Dev_Run at 2026-11-08T03:22:28.525Z finished Phase_1 for `webllm/qwen3.5-0.8b-q4f32/nvidia` while the same Combination had since completed three Dev_Runs. Now `phase.ts` counts a failure record only when its run type is `locked` AND `transient` is false. The schema stays `llm-probe-failure-v1`; `run_kind` (it was already written by the run flow) and the new `transient` flag are optional fields, so every older line still parses.
- Legacy reading rule (`effectiveFailure` in `results.ts`): `run_kind` is the field if it is `dev` or `locked`; else a `run_id` that starts with `dev-` means dev; anything else, including no run ID, means locked (fail-safe: a failure that cannot be shown to be a Dev_Run is not ignored). `transient` is the field if boolean; else the transient-error matcher is applied to `detail`, `reason` and `message`. The matcher is the one from `783efc6`, moved unchanged to `eval/probe/src/transient.ts` (`preflight.ts` re-exports it). New records always carry `transient` (`appendFailure` fills it from the matcher when the caller gave none).
- Correction record: the original line of 03:22:28.525Z in `eval/results/failures.jsonl` is untouched. A second line was appended with schema `llm-probe-failure-correction-v1` (`combination`, `target_at`, `run_kind: dev`, `transient: true`, `reason`, `at`). `readFailures` merges corrections by `combination` + `target_at` (last one wins) and does not return the correction lines as failures. A test reads the committed file and asserts the original bytes are there and the record reads as dev + transient. Note: by the legacy rule alone this record already read as dev (its `run_id` starts with `dev-`) and transient (matcher); the correction makes it explicit.
- `probe phase-status` after the fix: Phase_1 in progress; `transformers.js/qwen3.5-0.8b-q4`, `transformers.js/qwen3.5-2b-q4`, `transformers.js/lfm2.5-1.2b-instruct-q4` finished by Exclusion_Record; `webllm/qwen3.5-0.8b-q4f32/nvidia` and `webllm/qwen3.5-2b-q4f32/nvidia` pending (needs D and S). The Report's Combination status and "Failed Combinations" list count only gate-relevant failures; dev/transient records are still listed, marked "not counted as a Combination failure".
- Locked_Run transient-error rules (Author's condition 2). Decided and implemented before any Locked_Run (`LOCKED_LOAD_RETRIES`, `LOCKED_LOAD_BACKOFF_MS` in `run.ts`):
  1. Automatic retry applies only to the model load of a Locked_Run, before the first Card request, and only when the load fails with `model_load_failed` and a message the transient matcher recognises (`network error`, `Failed to fetch`, `net::ERR_*`, `ECONNRESET`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN`, `socket hang up`).
  2. At most 3 retries (4 loads in all), with a wait of 5 s, 15 s and 45 s before retries 1, 2 and 3.
  3. Every retry closes the failed handle and opens a new one with a new Fresh_Profile (the Fresh_Profile hook runs again). A retry never reuses a half-filled cache or the byte counter of a failed attempt, which is why a plain second `load()` on the same handle was rejected: the counter is not reset, so the download figures would be tainted.
  4. Cold-start and download figures come only from the first load that succeeded, in the Fresh_Profile opened for that load. Failed attempts write no perf record. When more than one load was needed, the perf record carries `load_attempts` (the count), so the Report reader can see it.
  5. Each failed attempt writes a failure record `run_kind: locked`, `transient: true`, `will_retry: true`, `attempt: n`. The gate ignores it. These are attempt notes, not Combination failures.
  6. If the last retry also fails transiently, the run stops as any load failure does (not_run records, ledger abort `model_load_failed`, a final locked + transient failure record the gate ignores). The Combination is not marked failed. Continuing it is `locked-run --resume <entry-id>`; no new Author approval mechanism is added, and per task 21.6 the resume is made only after asking the Author again.
  7. A transient error after the first request (mid-run, for example a network error reported as a load-class error) is never retried automatically: the run stops, the failure record is flagged transient (so the gate ignores it), and the run is continued only with `--resume`, after asking the Author again. A Fresh_Profile failure before the ledger `start` is not retried by this rule and, unchanged, uses no once-only slot.
  8. A load failure that is not transient (for example `weights missing`, out of memory) is not retried and counts for the gate, as before.
  Tests: `tests/unit/run.transient.test.ts` (two transient failures then success: 2 sleeps, 3 handles, 3 Fresh_Profiles, perf from the third handle with `load_attempts: 3`, gate ignores both records; no retry beyond the limit: 4 loads, ledger abort, no perf file; non-transient: no retry, counted; mid-run transient: stops, not counted; first-try load: no `load_attempts`). The browser retry path itself (a real second Chrome) is not exercised by a test; the fake runtime stands in for it.
- Report notes (Author's condition 3), `DEV_CONFOUND_NOTE` in `report.ts`, printed at the start of the Dev_Run section and tested: in the dev set the severe option is last in card order for every card that has one, because option rotation was applied only to the locked set (an oversight on the card-authoring side; the cards are locked and unchanged). Per the Author, the locked set's severe options are last 14, middle 26, first 7; so the position-versus-content distinction is to be drawn from the Locked_Run results. I did not open or compute anything from the locked files. Check of `dev.jsonl` only: 20 D cards, 18 with four options and 2 unscored two-option Sanity_Cards; 15 scored four-option cards have exactly one severe option, and it is the fourth in card order for all 15; the 3 other four-option cards have none. The two Sanity_Cards also list their severe option last (17 D cards in total with a severe option, all last). So the earlier "15 of 18 four-option cards" and the Author's "15 D cards with a severe option, all last" agree; the only difference is that the Sanity_Cards add 2 unscored cards with the same pattern.
- Author's approvals recorded here (task 21.1 dispatch): Locked_Run 21.2 (`webllm/qwen3.5-0.8b-q4f32/nvidia`) and Locked_Run 21.3 (`webllm/qwen3.5-2b-q4f32/nvidia`), each `--task DS`, at most 408 requests. These are the approvals of the start; neither run was started in this entry. The start and end entries of each run come when it runs.
- Author's condition 4: after the Locked_Runs, I report the Phase_1 conclusion first, and only then ask for Phase_2 approval, with a budget estimate that covers both D and S on Workers AI.
- No Locked_Run was started and no Workers AI call was made. `eval/cards/` and `locked.jsonl` were not opened (only `dev.jsonl` for the confound check).

### Spec: llm-probe — Property 40 flake fixed: the test's expectation was wrong (2026-11-09 06:20Z)

- Replayed seed 1120750890 on the clean tree: it shrinks to plan `timeouts {72: busy}`, `failRebuild: true`, failing at `0 !== 1` on `metrics.tasks[0].illegal.num` in `engine-faults.property.test.ts`.

In the synthetic plan, offset 72 is `D-sanity-901` (a Sanity_Card, base only). The code was right; the test counted cards the Metrics exclude. The seed only failed when the random plan put a Timeout (with a failed rebuild) on one of the few Sanity_Cards.
- Fix: the expected count now only includes Cards that are scored and not void. The plan from the seed is kept as an explicit `examples` entry of the property, so it runs on every gate run. No source file changed.

### Spec: llm-probe — second pre-existing flake found, not fixed (2026-11-09 06:22Z)

- `Property 32: Results records of every kind round trip byte-exact` (`results.property.test.ts`) failed once in a gates run with seed 286421559: the generated header has `template_hashes: {"__proto__": ""}`. `parseHeader` (and the `template_hashes` readers in `ledger.ts` and `ingest.ts`) build the map with `map[k] = value`, which does not create an own property for the key `__proto__`, so the round trip loses it. Real template names never use that key, so no run is affected; the fix (build with `Object.fromEntries` or `Object.defineProperty`) was left out of this work because it was not asked for. The next gates run was green.

### Spec: life-sim — deaths: the estate is settled before the Life flips (2026-11-11)

- Design "Deaths" orders sub-step 1 (`life = Dead { death }`) before sub-step 4 (inheritance and `Escheat`). The `Life::Dead` variant carries no balance and both Money_Flows name the deceased as the payer, so `economy::flow` (the only writer of balances) cannot move an estate whose owner is already `Dead`. `death.rs` therefore rolls every death first and then settles each death in Person ID order as: `death` Event, estate while the balance still exists, Debts, non-kin Relations, and finally `Life::Dead`, the emptied-Household removal and the waiting Soul. The final state and the Event order are what the design specifies (the `death` Event keeps a lower ID than every `inheritance` it causes); only the order of same-tick writes inside one settlement differs. Recorded for the Kiro audit (task 16); no design or requirement text changed.

### Spec: life-sim — births: trait-inheritance split and newborn wage (2026-11-11)

- Design "Births" step 2 says each of a newborn's Traits is "by roll, either a copy of one parent's trait or a fresh draw" but fixes no probability, and R10.5 only requires the draws to be seeded and keyed by the newborn's Person ID. `births.rs` draws uniformly among the mother, her living spouse (when there is one) and the fresh weighted draw (`params::draw_trait`), one source-choice site per trait: one parent gives a 1/2 copy chance, two parents 2/3. The newborn's `wage` is likewise not in the design's field list; it is drawn in `Params::wage_min..=wage_max` from the `Births` stream keyed by the newborn, matching the Opening_World rule. Both choices are deterministic; recorded for the Kiro audit (task 16). No design or requirement text changed.
- The stale assertion in `tests/properties.rs` ("no births or deaths yet: steps 3 to 11 are still empty", written in task 3.3) described the stub state and fails once births exist; replaced by the R9.3 soul-conservation count (Residents plus waiting Souls equal Total_Souls), which holds for any run.

### Spec: life-sim — outsider releases; the short batch returns to 2,000 ticks (2026-11-11)

- Step 3 is implemented in `outsiders.rs`: every waiting Soul other than the Player_Soul with `T - since > MAX_WAIT` (1,095 days) is released in Soul ID order into an outsider body. The body kind is a seeded roll per Soul (`rebuilt_share_ppm`, OP-4 A), the age is in 18..=40, the Traits come from the shared weighted draw keyed by the new Person, the name comes from the picker with a surname drawn for the arrival, the money is an `ArrivalEndowment` source in the new single-person Household, and no Relations are created (R11.2).
- With step 3 in place the reason for the shorter acceptance run is gone: `scripts/gates.sh`'s short batch line is back to `--ticks 2000`, and the temporary 1,000-ticks comment (recorded under "batch acceptance length before task 7.3" and checkpoint 5) is removed. `cargo run -q --release -p sim-cli -- batch --seeds 1..=20 --ticks 2000` prints 20 `ok` lines and `batch: 20/20 seeds ok`.
- Only `fixtures/parity/seed2-pairwise.replay.json` changed when the fixtures were regenerated: the other two fixture seeds produce no release inside their 2,000 ticks. `scripts/regen-fixtures.sh` was run twice and the second run left `git status` unchanged.

### Spec: life-sim — fault injection: soul conservation (9.3) (2026-11-11)

- Fault: in `death.rs` `settle_death`, the Soul entry was removed (`world.souls.places.remove(&soul)`) instead of being set to `SoulPlace::Waiting { since: death_tick }`.
- Failure seen, first run: `cargo test -p sim-core --test invariants` failed through the independent Total_Souls assertion in `life_gen` (9.3); `batch --seeds 1..=5 --ticks 2000` failed on every seed but reported `criterion=9.4 detail: soul counter is 53 but the World holds 51 souls` (ticks 133, 208, 1124, 1015, 139). The checker compared the counter only with the current place count, and its R9.3 check compared Residents plus waiting Souls with that same count, so neither noticed the missing Soul.
- Strengthened `check_souls`: the place count must now equal `opening_residents + initial_waiting` (Total_Souls), reported as 9.3 (commit `ae51670`). Repeated the injection: every seed prints `criterion=9.3 detail: Total_Souls is 51, expected 52` at the same ticks, and the property test fails at its 9.3 assertion.
- Reverted with `git checkout -- crates/sim-core/src/death.rs`; `git status --short` empty; both commands pass again (invariants: 3 passed; batch: `5/5 seeds ok`).

### Spec: life-sim — outsider surname rule (task 17.1, 2026-11-11)

- `outsiders.rs` now picks the arrival surname from the surnames no living Resident uses: the indices of `world.derived.living_names` in a `BTreeSet<u16>`, the free indices `0..SURNAME_COUNT` in ascending order, `free[below(draw, count)]` with the existing `RELEASE_SURNAME` draw keyed by the released Soul; with every surname in use it falls back to `below(draw, SURNAME_COUNT)` over all 60. The first name still comes from `pick_full_name` with `RELEASE_NAME`. The rule lives in the pure helper `outsider_surname(draw, used)`, and the module doc states it.
- Unit tests: a free surname is never one in `used` (sparse set and 59 of 60 used, several draws); the all-60 fallback equals `below(draw, 60)`; after a World-level release the newcomer's surname is used by no other living Resident; two clones released at the same tick get the same `FullName`.

### Spec: life-sim — Property 6 expectation fix (commit f058096, logged late, 2026-11-11)

- Property 6 (`crates/sim-core/tests/history.rs`) compared a repayment's payer with the Debt's debtor at the start of the tick. A death earlier in the same tick can transfer the Debt first (`debt_transfer` keeps the open amount and changes the debtor), so the expected payer is the debtor after the last `debt_transfer` before the repayment.
- The case was found by a full-file run at seed 6399358489806569765 and is kept in `crates/sim-core/tests/history.proptest-regressions` (`seed: 6399358489806569765, residents: 58, params: Stress`, four `Act` inputs).
- The fix changed the test expectation, not simulation code.
- This entry is written late, at the audit's request (`docs/life-sim-audit.md`); no earlier entry was edited.

### Spec: underworld — task 4.1 offerings (2026-11-13)

- New `underworld/offerings.rs`: `process_offerings` runs as tick step 5, after deaths, so a death in step 4 gets its funeral offering in the same tick. For every Ghost in Person ID order (`ghosts::ghosts`), the occasion factor is the largest of the funeral `funeral_factor` (2) on the death tick, the anniversary `anniversary_factor` (1) every 365 days after it, and Halloween `halloween_factor` (1) when `T % 365 == halloween_day` (0).
- Eligible offerers are living Residents aged 12+ with a Relation toward the Ghost of affinity at least `offer_min_affinity` (1), in Person ID order. The amount follows design "Offerings" exactly: `a * (piety + 3) * (2 + min(money / offer_money_step, offer_money_max_steps)) * factor / 12`, floored and clamped to 0..=500. The largest possible product is 6,000, so the floor division is exact on non-negative integers.
- An amount of at least 1 appends one `offering` Event with tag `joss_paper`, `magnitude` the full amount and `credited` from `joss::credit`; an Event whose credit the cap reduces is still appended with its full magnitude (R2.4, R2.7). The credit is computed before the append and applied after it, so a refused append (exhausted Event counter) credits nothing. No money moves (R2.8); a reborn Soul leaves the queue, so its dead body is no Ghost and gets nothing.
- Unit tests: the formula at 0, 1 and 500 plus the factor and money boundary, funeral and Halloween on one tick counting once with factor 2, a reborn Soul's dead body getting no offering, no money balance changing, and the credit stopping at the cap while the magnitude stays full.
- Checksums change because the new Events enter the log: the replay fixtures end at `c14fa7c81d817f31`, `e82abcb0c47171fb`, `5e3a0cef54686819`; the acceptance batch ends at `74d7fbaef6205a73`, `d1f9d4f2dab4cb2a`, `e09ec6bb8ef5dfc1`, `35a9f505442bea77`, `04e29c33d1a6f4aa`. ### Spec: underworld — invariants and the property suite (2026-11-13)

- `InvariantChecker` gained the design's underworld checks with the `U` labels: `U1.2` and `U1.3` (one account per Soul, each ledger field attributable to one Event and one Soul, and the per-tick balance identity `previous + credits - spends`), `U2.5` and `U2.6` (the per-Soul per-Cap_Year credits and haunting/Rebuilt spends folded from the log stay at or below `yearly_cap`, and the account's own counters equal that fold for the Cap_Year they belong to), `U4.3` and `U5.3` (a `dream`/`haunting` names a target alive and connected to the acting Ghost at the append, allowing a death later in the same tick), and `U15.1` plus `U15.4` to `U15.8` (the Magistrate unchanged, in no Household/Relation/Debt/property/Soul_Place, no rule Event, and only ever the second actor of `appeal`/`offering`). Life-sim check `5.8` keeps its code and uses the extended Afterlife set; `5.7` now accepts the one official Person as a known actor, because its recipient-only rule is `U15.8`.
- The stateful parts are the previous Joss_Balances, the per-Soul per-Cap_Year counter folds and the opening Magistrate; `new()` folds the opening log against an empty baseline (Opening_World generation leaves every balance at 0).
- Batch (`--seeds 1..=5 --ticks 29200 --require-targets`) passes with the extended checker; every seed prints `invariants=pass` and the same figures as before this spec's test phase, so the new folds agree with the recorded state on 146,000 ticks.
- Generator (`tests/underworld_gen/mod.rs`): a scenario is a seed, an opening size in 40..=60 and `Params::stress_underworld()` in three cases of four. Each tick plans a state-aware mix from the World's own state — valid and invalid `Act`, dream, haunting, Bribe, slot claim, Carry_Over and `Choose` payloads, with every valid `Choose` option taken from `preview_node` — submits them as ordinary `TickInput`s, returns the plan with its outcomes and runs the extended checker after the tick. The smoke test over 20 generated runs shows at least one dream, haunting, Bribe, Birth claim, Standing claim, Carry_Over, External_Choice and R8.1 placement (the generator plans no claim in every fourth run, so the placement bound is reached).
- Bug found by Property 10 and fixed in this task group, not a design choice: `nodes::clamp_access` clamped a grant to `now..=current`, which *raised* `access_from` when the register had already opened in the past (`current < now`), contradicting design "Bribes" ("a grant moves `access_from` no later than it was") and R6.6. The range is empty in that case now, so the value stays as it is. No fixture checksum changes (the parity replays carry no Bribe).
- Formulation notes, logged because the end-of-tick World does not show the state each step read (they bound what the properties can observe, and none of them removes an assertion the design asks for): Property 3 computes the step-5 offerer set from the end-of-tick Relations (an `Act` of the same tick can have changed the affinity in step 2a, and step 13 decay moves it one point toward 0, so on a decay tick both readings are candidates), reads the money step from the start-of-tick balance and widens it to `0..=max` only for an heir of a death in the same tick, and skips the pair of a dream and of such an heir; the pair set, the one-Event-per-pair rule, the `joss_paper` tag and the amount formula are asserted for every other pair. Properties 8 to 10 compare a tick in which the tested input is the only underworld input with the same tick without it (the other inputs would react to the resulting balance), and compare the tick's Event card types rather than Event IDs, because an appended Event shifts every later ID (Debts are keyed by loan Event IDs, so they are compared by content).
- Property 9's Mood expectation folds the documented `mood_delta` rows of the tick's Events in log order with the clamp after each row: a haunting at a Mood of -100 does not move it, so "without - 15" would be wrong.
- Property 16 re-runs the recorded stream in a fresh `Sim` and compares every Checksum, and also exercises `replay::record`/`verify` plus a tampered Checksum (the file format path); `record` has no Params parameter, so the stress runs use the `Sim` path.
- Property 19 runs `life_gen::CoreChecker` and `life_gen::check_structure` on generated underworld runs at every tick, so the life-sim invariants hold under underworld inputs; the two life-sim expectations the underworld changed (the queue rules, the Soul choice at the slot's birth tick) are covered by `U7.10` and by Property 11 here.

### Spec: underworld — Kiro's review of the 10.1 stop and 6.15, Author's decisions, spec changes (2026-11-15)

- Context: the agent stopped task 10.1 under OP-U13 step 6 (`rebuilt_claims=0` after the offering-scale and rebuilt-price levers; median Player_Wait credit 6.5) and left 6.15 open (U2.5, U15.8 and extended 5.8 produced failures other than the target label). Its 10.1 and 6.15 entries were still uncommitted in the working tree when Kiro wrote this one; Kiro committed only this entry and left the agent's lines and `crates/sim-core/tests/underworld.proptest-regressions` unstaged.
- Correction of Kiro's design (estimate errors): the Params rationale said life-sim decay pulls kin affinity to 0 "over decades"; step 11 moves affinity 1 point per 30 days, so kin relations starting at 30–60 reach 0 in about 2.5–5 years unless refreshed. The reachability estimate ("four Relations at affinity 40 … about 160 at the funeral") ignored this and was unfounded. Kiro's rough arithmetic (not measured): social events touch each directed Relation about once per decade. Also found: the Auto_Player submits no `Act` while the player is alive, so batches measure a player who never tends relations; a Rebuilt_Body has no unique benefit over an Imported_Vessel (same body, higher price, counts against the cap), so it is strictly dominated.
- Author's decisions: (1) Rebuilt_Body option A: this spec delivers the correct path only, records that it has no unique benefit and that Carry_Over is not customization; paid customization of part of the rebuilt body is a committed delivery bound to spec 6 with acceptance targets (structure.md item 6; product.md rebirth roles). (2) H1–H5 offering diagnosis approved: default Params, seeds 1..=5, 29,200 ticks; distinguish natural decay to zero, real feuds (by change source, not by the mere presence of a negative event), offerers lost by death, and the return on tending relations; the Devoted_Branch is a control branch with changed inputs (at most one legal Help/Gift per 30 days, fixed target rule, recorded investment), a diagnostic budget, not a game rule; report absolute figures, no X-times threshold. Offering mechanism M-A/M-B/M-C not chosen (OP-U15); calibration paused. (3) Gate split: functional coverage, ordinary-world balance, reachability after investment; Rebuilt_Body claims leave the passive zero-count hard gate and get a targeted functional test (R11.13); the rest of the list and the reachability thresholds wait for the diagnosis (OP-U14, R11.14 report-only). (4) C1+C2 evidence contract for R12.4: C1 the checker recognises a directly built illegal state with the exact label; C2 the prescribed production fault causes a failure, earlier guards allowed, no guard disabled; compile errors, timeouts, interruptions and unrelated failures do not count; earlier records are judged one by one, not in bulk.
- Spec changes: requirements (Out of scope note, R7.11, R11.9, R11.12, new R11.13 and R11.14, R12.4 rewritten, new R12.5 and R12.6, Devoted_Branch, OP-U14, OP-U15); design (dated corrections, Rebuilt scope note, "Offering diagnosis (H1–H5)", gate split with a placeholder `ZERO_COUNT_LIST`, C1/C2 table with Kiro's provisional re-judging of the earlier 6.15 records, calibration steps 4–6 suspended); tasks (STOP rule; 6.16 targeted Rebuilt test; 6.15 split into 6.15a C1 and 6.15b C2 with STOP; 9.5 diagnosis with STOP; 9.6, 10.x, 11.x, 12.1 blocked on OP-U14/OP-U15); steering product.md and structure.md. `validate_spec_format`: no issues on all three. ### Spec: underworld — Author's correction: full bribe atomicity for F2 (2026-11-15)

- The Author found that Kiro's F2 contract (Event ID room only) did not meet R6.2 and LS-R1.5: a non-ID refusal of the Appeal after the BribeOffering and the spend still leaves partial state, and the U15.8 fault had already shown that path. Kiro had written that residual into the design instead of closing it.
- New F2 contract: before any write or spend, check the complete append preconditions of both Events; write both and spend only when both succeed; on any refusal no Event, no spend, no node and no Checksum change. One source of validation: `World::check_append` is extracted from `World::append` (which calls it, accepting and refusing as before), `EventLog::has_room(n)` checks ID room, and `World::append_all` checks every Event against the pre-batch World and then writes all; `magistrate::commit_bribe` runs validate → `append_all` → spend → fire node. F1's `debug_assert!` stays a diagnostic guard only. Tests: `a_bribe_on_a_near_exhausted_event_counter_is_rejected_atomically`, `append_all_refuses_a_swapped_appeal_and_writes_nothing`, `a_bribe_with_a_swapped_appeal_spends_nothing_and_fires_no_node`. Batch checksums and fixtures must stay unchanged; the agent stops if they change or if `append`'s behaviour would have to change.
- Design choice reported to the Author: `check_append` takes no `tags` parameter because `World::append` checks no tags today (an unused parameter would fail clippy).
- Spec changes: design (dated correction under "Append refusals in the input handlers (F1, F2)"), tasks (6.18 decision line with the new steps). `validate_spec_format`: no issues. Order unchanged: 6.15b U15.8 batch → 6.17 → 6.18.

### Spec: first-playable — Author's P-1 execution scope decision (2026-11-16)

- Author decided P-1 execution scope after OMP laid out three placements of the rule. Chosen: **B, the Sim_Worker guard plus disabled controls**, covering **every** interactive Player_Node, with `chooser_absent` kept. Rejected: A (UI-only disablement, contract untestable because `?harness=1` or any direct Worker call still advances) and C (`sim-core` waits). OMP's evidence against C: the passive acceptance batch (`--seeds 1..=5 --ticks 29200 --require-targets`) has no answerer, so a waiting core never reaches 29,200 ticks and the `first_stop_band` gate of R13.5, this spec's only hard narrator gate, dies with it; R15.2 also requires a replay stream in which a Player_Node resolves by Rules_Default, which C cannot construct.
- Why the conflict dissolved rather than being traded off: R8.3 already stops the Worker after the firing tick at every Speed, so the only path to a defaulted interactive node is the player pressing Run/Step again without choosing. That is a Worker/UI behaviour, not a core one. The "how do we tell a real player from scripted CLI input" question in the handoff text was a non-problem: `controller.ts` lives in `web/src/worker/`, and `sim-cli` depends only on `sim-core`, so the separation is structural and needs no runtime execution-mode flag. OMP also noted the same shape already exists in steering `tech.md` (LLM boundary: the presentation layer waits, the rules default stays in the rules layer), so B is not a new convention.
- Why the gate covers every node rather than only the first, against the literal instruction: "first node only" needs the Worker to know that a node is the first of the first life, which the Snapshot does not carry; supplying it means either a new core field plus property or the UI inferring it from the Chronicle. The uniform rule needs no new state. Every family already carries an explicit passive option (`ignore_it`, `wait_it_out`, `let_it_go`, `stay_away`, `keep_it`), so blocking Run removes no player expression: doing nothing stays available as a recorded choice instead of a silent default.
- Author's three implementation contracts, added on top of the decision: the answered flag means accepted-and-pending-resolution only (never "the client sent something"), a rejected submission keeps the gate closed; the Run/Step guard is atomic per request, with no partial advance from a repeated Run, a repeated choice or an invalid choice, and `create` must cancel the old World's pending requests and timer callbacks so no stale response writes into the new World; the fault injection must drive the real Worker request path, not the disabled DOM control, and after the revert the normal smoke, native/WASM parity and fixture must be unchanged.
- **Defect OMP found in its own first draft of the gate, from contract 1.** OMP had put the answered flag in the Snapshot as `player_node.external`. Reading the code showed `InputStream` lives in `Sim` (`crates/sim-core/src/tick.rs:266-271`), not in `World`, and `snapshot_json` takes `&World` (`crates/sim-core/src/snapshot.rs:147`), while `narrator.pending.external` is only written at 2a of t+1. A World-only Snapshot would therefore still read "unanswered" immediately after an accepted submission, which is exactly the deadlock the Author's contract 1 warns against. ### Spec: first-playable — the first-stop band is half-open (2026-11-16)

- The executing session flagged that checkpoint C1 said the first stop fires "inside 600..=900" while the design's trigger window is 600..=870 and `first_interrupt_max` is 900. Three different numbers were in play and none of the documents said which comparison is inclusive.
- Traced it. The glossary defined the band as "`first_interrupt_min` to `first_interrupt_max` inclusive", Requirement 3.1 set `first_interrupt_max` to 30 × Play_Rate = 900, and the design's batch report printed the band as `600..=900`. So the documents did say 900 was inside, in three places, and the design's own "Values" paragraph also called 900 "30 s". The executing session's reading (900 should be outside) is the one that matches the words "within 30 seconds": at 30 ticks per second, offset 900 is reached at 30.0 s, which is no longer *within* 30 s. Offset 899 is the last tick inside it.
- Author's instruction was to look and fix if needed, so OMP fixed it rather than asking. The band is now `600 <= offset < 900`, written `600..=899`, in the glossary, Requirement 3.1, the design's "Values" paragraph and the batch report line. The trigger window stays `[600, 870]`; offsets 871..=899 remain inside the band for a candidate that fires before the Intro_Debt's own trigger. The 20 to 30 s figure is stated as the wall-clock target of Requirement 16.11 and not a tick bound.
- One consequence worth naming: the firing rule only has a lower bound. `first_interrupt_max` is not a firing condition, so a first node that becomes eligible after offset 899 still fires, and the upper bound is enforced by the `first_stop_band` gate failing, not by the Narrator suppressing the node. The design's budget-check paragraph now says so. Previously it only showed `T − start ≥ first_interrupt_min`, so a reader could have added the upper bound to the firing rule and silently dropped late stops.
- The fault injection for that gate was self-defeating as written: it required `T − start > first_interrupt_max` before the first fire, which with an inclusive bound of 900 meant the injected code fired at offset 901 or later and the assertion could pass for the wrong reason. It now requires `T − start ≥ first_interrupt_max`, so the earliest injected first fire is offset 900, exactly one past the band.
- C1's run instruction changed with it. "Run to tick 900" would clip the observation at the boundary, so a stop at offset 901 would show up as "none" and hide the real number. It now says to run past offset 900 and report the real offset, and that an offset of 900 fails.
- No code was run. The three spec files and this log are still uncommitted WIP.

### Spec: first-playable — task 1.1 file scope and the undesignated opening state (2026-11-16)

- The executing session stopped before task 1.1 and reported that its file list does not compile. Confirmed against the code. `opening::generate` builds the `World` with a struct literal (`crates/sim-core/src/opening.rs:143`) and `testing::apply` destructures it with every field named and no `..` (`crates/sim-core/src/testing.rs:181`), so adding `World::narrator` fails both files, and neither was in task 1.1's list. The same shape repeats for `intro_debt` in task 3.1, which also listed neither `world.rs` (the field and its `Canon` impl) nor `lib.rs` (the module declaration).
- Fixed in `tasks.md` only, no code. Task 1.1 gains `opening.rs` and `testing.rs`, restricted to one line each: `narrator: Narrator::default()`. The task text now says outright that no opening rule, no body selection, no added Debt and no `intro_debt` belong to 1.1. Task 3.1 gains `lib.rs`, `world.rs` and `testing.rs`, and states that `intro_debt` is declared on `World`, encoded immediately after `debts`, and added to both exhaustive destructures.
- The second point was a real hole, not just a missing file. `generate` writes the struct literal before step 9c designates the Debt, and the design's `IntroDebt` had only `Grace { loan, body }` and `Ended { loan }`. `Grace` has to name a loan that does not exist yet, so the literal cannot write it, and the spec left the executing agent to invent the third state. Added `IntroDebt::Undesignated`, which names no loan and no body. `generate` sets it in the literal; step 9c is the only writer of `Grace` and overwrites it; `intro::update` is the only writer of `Ended`; nothing writes `Undesignated` again. `generate` returns only after 9c, so no World that escapes it, and no tick boundary, is ever `Undesignated`. It is a construction-time variant, not a third gameplay state, which is why it does not change Requirements 5.8 to 5.11: those speak about a finished opening. Property 19 now also asserts the state is never `Undesignated` at a tick end.

### Spec: first-playable — task 7.1 web pacing scope and design clarifications (2026-11-18)

- Replaced the browser controller's Speed-ticks-per-Frame loop with the pure wall-time pacer and `run_until_stop`; `PLAY_RATE` is 30 and Speed is a multiplier. Tick counts alone cross the WASM boundary. The native/WASM Snapshot DTO fields agree with the design's new blocks; card Person IDs (including `underworld_view.connected`) are numbers, while Node IDs, ticks and slot tokens retain their Snapshot string forms. No Rust, fixture, dependency, lockfile or spec checkbox change is part of this web task.
- Adopted the task's integer-cap and re-anchor-frame clarifications: an integer batch count must be no larger than `max(1, speed × 30 / 20)`, so fractional caps round down (1, 10, 547 at Speed 1, 7, 365). Re-anchoring runs zero ticks on that frame. Starting or resuming run resets the anchor; a changed Speed while running also resets it, avoiding the negative-due stall when lowering Speed. The Speed-change anchor lifecycle is a design clarification for planning review at C3, not a new simulation rule.
- Main approved a necessary interpretation of Property 21: "total allowed by batch caps" is the independent recurrence `total_k = min(target_k, total_(k-1) + cap)`, not accumulated unused frame capacity. For example, Speed 1 frames at 16 ms and 100 ms run 0 then 1 tick, not 2 ticks; the normative Clock pacing formula does not bank an idle frame's cap. The generated total-count property uses monotonic frame times and an independent total-count reference; backward-time/nonnegative cases are separate. An integer-interval refresh-rate example checks the same duration at 4/8/16/32 ms intervals.
- Main resolved the reply/stop carrier gap without a third field: every automatic stop, including one caused by `step`, posts one unthrottled status with `snapshot.stop`; a stopped step also echoes the same payload in its one reply. A running `pause` replies with `snapshot.stop = { reasons: ['user'], world }` and no extra status; an already-paused `pause` carries no stop. Later messages do not repeat the stop. Task 8.1/9.1 must make scene consumption of the step's status/reply pair idempotent by `(worldId, tick)`. Reply `world?` stays available for task 8.1's read/submission handlers.
- Main approved Snapshot-form request identifiers: numeric dreamer Person IDs, decimal-string node IDs, option tokens, Snapshot slot tokens and nullable Trait Carry_Over; Customization keeps v5 payload JSON. The seven task-8.1 request kinds are typed but have no handlers yet. Inspection found no existing unsupported-request path, so Main approved seven explicit transitional branches replying `invalid-state` / `unsupported request: <type>` once with current cached state, without touching the handle, reading the clock or changing the anchor. Task 8.1 replaces them; truly unknown malformed message types retain their existing behavior.
- Mechanical Files-list closure: shared request typing and routing in `main/sim-client.ts` and `main/harness.ts`, the multiplier comment in `main/ui-state.ts`, and unit `helpers/{fakes,gen,reference,wasm}.ts`. No UI layout/presentation or interactive unanswered-node gate was implemented. The TypeScript LSP tool reported no available server, so the required reference queries could not run; compilation is the caller-closure check. The old generated controller request budget could admit zero frame commands at its 3,000-tick limit; the migrated generator now includes bounded paced frames, preserving and exercising the scheduling coverage.

### Spec: first-playable — task 7.1 pacing, protocol and smoke rulings (2026-11-18)

- The executing session stopped task 7.1 with its web work uncommitted (HEAD `c0085b1`) and asked for rulings on six design gaps and one conflict with the existing smoke specs. OMP read the uncommitted `pacer.ts`, `controller.ts` and `protocol.ts`, the two smoke specs, `playwright.config.ts`, the handoff and the saved gate output under `$HOME/.cache/back-in-the-family/first-playable/7.1/`, and ran nothing. - Item 1, the anchor's life: ratified. The anchor is reset when a `run` is accepted, when `set-speed` changes the Speed while running, and on a backlog of more than one second, and the re-anchoring Frame runs no tick. The Speed-change case is needed because `ran` is counted at the old Speed; the session's two examples follow from the formula (one second at 365 then Speed 1 leaves `due` at −10,920 and about 364 s to wait).
- Item 2, the batch cap: not ratified as rounded down; rewritten to `maxBatch = ceil(speed × 30 / 20)`, which is 2, 11, 45, 135 and 548. The session was right that only rounding down met Property 21 as it stood, and right about its cost: one tick per Frame at Speed 1 keeps pace only at 30 Frames per second or more. The cap exists to bound a catch-up, not to make pace depend on the refresh rate, which Requirement 8.1 rules out, so the property was wrong and is changed. Rounded up, a Frame gap of at most 50 ms loses no tick at any Speed, because `floor(x + d) − floor(x) <= ceil(d)`. This is derived, not measured in a browser.
- Item 3, Property 21's total: ratified as the per-Frame recurrence `total_k = min(target_k, total_(k−1) + maxBatch)`; "the total allowed by the batch caps" was undefined and the sum-of-caps reading contradicts the pacing formula. The property now also states the consequence that makes it more than a restatement of the function: Frames at most 50 ms apart keep the total equal to the target.
- Item 4, the stop carriers: rewritten. The session's interim reading put a stopped `step`'s reasons in a status and again in its reply, and left the page to match the two by World and tick. A tick's stop now goes out in one status only, posted before the reply of the request that ran the tick, and no reply carries it; a `pause` that ends a running period carries `['user']` and the Snapshot in its reply and posts no status; a `pause` while paused carries no stop. The design sentence "`step` ... reports stops in its reply" is replaced. Requirement 8.4 already asked for a status and needed no change.
- Item 5, request fields: ratified. Requests carry identifiers in the Snapshot's form and only the controller builds payload JSON. The same ruling fills what the design had left open for task 8.1: `Snapshot.playerNode` carries the gate's read to the page, replies carry `world` or `checksums`, the three failure kinds `rejected`, `sim-error` and `invalid-tick` are kept apart, and `this.pending` is also refreshed after a plain `submit`, which can queue a `ChoosePlayer`.
- Item 6, the seven typed-but-unhandled requests answered `invalid-state` in the task 7.1 commit: noted as a state between two commits of one phase. None of those branches may remain after task 8.1.
- Item 7, the existing smoke specs. The facts are the session's: `scripts/gates.sh` exited 1 after 503.130 s on the last gate; `fixture.spec.ts` timed out at 120 s with the page at tick 641, paused, the Pause control disabled; `responsive.spec.ts` finished Speed 1 only before the 170 s bound; and the built WASM, driven directly, stops that World at `tick()` 641 and 1660, both `player_node`, with all 2,000 Checksums equal to the fixture when its inputs are submitted. The cause is in the plan, not in the code: first-playable changed what a running World does and the tasks did not carry the two older specs along. Ruled as Requirements 16.12 and 16.13. `responsive.spec.ts` keeps all five Speeds and measures each from tick 0 to the first stop or 10 s, with the long-task observer left on through the stop, since the stop's World Snapshot is the new load on the Main_Thread. `fixture.spec.ts` step 6 becomes a Speed 1 run paused by the control and a Speed 365 run to the automatic stop. Both belong to the task 7.1 commit, so that commit is green. From task 8.1 the two stepped runs end at the first `node_unanswered`; answering the node for the fixture is not an option, because the Chronicle source is inside the Checksum. The Playwright bounds stay as they are until task 14.
- What the smoke ruling gives up, stated so it is not mistaken for coverage: the browser no longer compares ticks 642 to 2,000 of `seedbig-pairwise` once the gate exists (native against WASM still does, and the playthrough Smoke_Test will through the Worker on its own fixture), and nothing measures cadence or long tasks over a long run at Speeds 7 to 365 in a late World. Whether the playthrough Smoke_Test should report its longest Main_Thread task is left to the Author; it is not in the tasks.

### Spec: first-playable — World refresh between stops ruled (2026-11-18)

- The executing session asked, with task 9.1 committed (`3abc459`, `4a2ef34`), whether the Town_View updates between stops: Requirements 9.1 and 9.2 say only "the latest Snapshot", and the design did not say when the page gets one. OMP read `controller.ts`, `protocol.ts`, `ui-state.ts` and `App.svelte` and ran nothing. The session's facts hold in the code: a `create-world` reply and a running `status` carry no World, and the page reads one `world-snapshot` after creating. Its own page run shows the result, status tick 48 over a World of tick 0.
- Ruled, as Requirement 9.9, the design's "World delivery to the page" and new task 9.2: the page reads the World again while running, once for every ten `status` messages (at most one a second under the 100 ms throttle), with one read outstanding at most, no timer and no clock; the Worker and the protocol are not changed. The read after `create-world` is ratified.
- Why, and what it does not buy. The reason is the waiting Player_Soul: its Joss_Balance and Needed lines change with no stop, so a panel that updates only at stops would have the player pause to learn whether a slot can be claimed. For the town the gain is small and is stated so that it is not taken for liveliness: in the committed `seed1-pairwise.snapshot-500.json`, 500 ticks into a World of 50, two of the opening Residents are gone and one newborn is listed, so at Speed 1 the 20 to 30 seconds before the first stop show about three marker changes. Moving markers is not in this spec.
- Two gaps found on the way, both in task 9.2. The reducer takes `stop.world` from a status and not from a reply, so the World a `pause` reply carries is dropped and a manual pause keeps the old World on screen; and a `step` that reports no stop leaves the World one tick behind, which the playthrough's fallback Step clicks would then assert against. The rule for both is that a paused page whose World is not of the displayed tick reads it once. Read in the code, not run.
- Task 9.1 itself is not reviewed here and its boxes are not checked. The spec edits were checked with a throwaway script, not Kiro's `validate_spec_format`.

### Spec: first-playable — task 9.2 current World delivery (2026-11-18)

- Implemented the ruled R9.9 delivery policy in the existing reducer and App. World precedence is successful `message.world`, otherwise `snapshot.stop.world`, on replies and statuses alike; the manual Pause carrier is no longer dropped. `worldSnapshotNeeded` is a pure reducer-state decision: paused stale Worlds request one read, running Worlds request on the tenth ordinary running status, one read remains outstanding across replacement until its reply finishes, and a failed read is not repeated at its requested tick. App marks the request before sending it and forwards its reply or transport failure into the same reducer; the separate Create-only mechanism is gone. No timer, clock, Worker, protocol, smoke spec, Playwright config, Rust, fixture or task-10 change was made.
- Main approved one pending spec-ratification deviation in design wording, not a new gameplay rule. R9.9 says "once for every ten status messages" and task 9.2's test contract says "reads are at least ten running statuses apart"; these observable requirements agree. Design's "since a World was last taken" counter description is equivalent on success but conflicts after a failed read. A running read consumes/resets its ten-status allowance when sent; every actual World carrier still resets the count. Failure at the same tick is not retried, and the next running attempt requires another ten running statuses. The success path and paused rule are unchanged. A focused test pins tenth status → failure → nine statuses without a read → tenth status permits one; this wording needs spec-side ratification, which this task does not edit.
- Concentrated acceptance ran once, serially, with every real exit 0: `mise exec -- pnpm --dir web run typecheck` 3.033 s (100 files, zero errors/warnings); web `test:unit` 1.543 s (100/100 tests, runner duration 1380.687254 ms); `scripts/web-build.sh` 1.111 s including its serial WASM build and deploy checks; web `test:smoke` 21.642 s; R15.6 against `2cabbaa` 0.002 s with no output. Complete outputs, actual exits and wall times are `/home/kaiki/.cache/back-in-the-family/first-playable/9.2/{typecheck,unit,web-build,smoke,r15-6}.{log,exit,seconds}`. No complete gates run was made.

The fixture acquired and compared 641 Checksums in each protocol/reference prefix. - Added nine focused examples and one unnumbered fast-check schedule test (1,000 cases): `R9.9: a manual pause adopts stop.world and reply.world takes precedence`; `R9.9: create requests one World and a non-stop Step requests the new tick`; `R9.9: a stop Step takes its status World and its reply requests no second read`; `R9.9: only the tenth running status requests a World; a carrier resets the count`; `R9.9: no second read while one is outstanding, even across statuses and a pause`; `R9.9: a failed running read consumes ten statuses before the next attempt`; `R9.9: failed reads are not repeated at the same paused or running tick`; `R9.9: replacement waits for the old read and ignores its World or rejection`; `R9.9: a transport failure marks its read tick and a stale failure cannot affect a new World`; `R9.9: generated event sequences keep reads single-flight, spaced and paused Worlds covered`. ### Spec: first-playable — window extended; decisions and facts for model access (2026-11-19)

- The Author extended the spec 6 window by one day: tasks 12.1 to 16.1 finish by 2026-11-22 at the latest. `tasks.md` says so, and `structure.md` follows in task 15.1.
- The Author gave permission, ahead of the next spec, for the deployment to gain a Worker script with a Workers AI binding. Nothing is deployed or pushed under spec 6.
- The Author restated the premise of the request budget. Players are encouraged to deploy their own copy from a one-click button in the README; the budget is designed to the Cloudflare Free plan so that an account that pays nothing can play; the public demo is there for the judges. The budget is therefore per deployment, and a deployment's own daily allocation is its cap. No counter shared across players is designed.
- Published limits, read on 2026-11-19 by a subagent from developers.cloudflare.com (Workers limits; Workers AI pricing, limits and errors; the clef model page; static assets billing). Workers AI: 10,000 neurons a day at no charge, reset at 00:00 UTC, and HTTP 429 with code 3036 once they are used. clef, `@cf/cloudflare/clef`: 21,818 neurons per million input tokens and no charge for output. Text generation: 300 requests a minute. Workers Free: 100,000 requests a day and 10 ms of CPU per request. Requests for static assets are free and do not run the Worker unless it is set to run first.
- From the llm-probe records (the Dev_Run and smoke results, and this log's settlements): a clef request took 729 to 1,076 input tokens, 920 on average, which is about 20 to 23 neurons, so a day's allocation is about 430 to 500 requests of that size. Those were probe cards; the size of a dream prompt in the game has not been measured. The latency of p50 600 ms and p95 940 ms was measured from a local Node process and not through a Worker. No 429 was recorded in 315 requests.
- One-click deploy does not work with the repository as it builds today, by the deploy-button and Workers Builds pages and the repository's build chain. A button on `web/` clones only that directory, and the WASM it needs is built from the Rust workspace above it into the git-ignored `target/wasm-pkg`. `web/package.json`'s `build` is `vite build` alone. The repository root has no package manifest and no Wrangler configuration. The documented Workers Builds image lists no Rust toolchain. The next spec has to choose how a deployable tree is published. Not tried: no hosted build and no button was run.
- Open, for the next spec to close: clef's license (the README records it as unverified, and the model page links a LICENSE file that was not opened); whether the Workers Rate Limiting binding is available on the Free plan (the pages read do not say); and what the local Wrangler token may do (`wrangler whoami` reports a login by API token and prints no scopes).

### Spec: first-playable — Author rulings on the model budget and llm-probe disclosure (2026-11-20)

- The Author approved the proposed model budget for the next spec: one model request per eligible decision node, no retry, and a 10 s timeout with Rules_Default on failure. The page allows 40 model requests per page session by default, configurable by the deployer. This is a page limit, not protection for the public endpoint. No app-level per-minute limit is in the approved baseline.
- The Worker rejects oversized requests, targeting no more than about 50 neurons per accepted request. Measure real in-game dream prompts before setting a byte limit; bytes are not a verified token bound. The daily ceiling is the Cloudflare Free account's shared 10,000 neurons, including local inference on that account, not a per-deployment quota. There is no separate daily counter. On quota exhaustion (HTTP 429, code 3036), play continues with Rules_Default and a daily-quota notice; the platform quota resets at 00:00 UTC. The earlier 430–500 request figure is an estimate for probe-sized inputs, not a guaranteed daily request count.
- The Author ruled that the disclosed access to the Locked_Run result does not change the llm-probe conclusions and requires no action on them. The disclosure stays on record. No locked or blind material is reopened and no probe is rerun.

### Judge demo release — expiry proof distinguishes wire TTL from Chromium clock adjustment

- The [MDN Expires documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Set-Cookie#expiresdate) and Chromium's `canonical_cookie.cc` describe browser clock-skew correction: stored expiry is wire expiry plus creation time minus response Date. Stored expiry is therefore not guaranteed to be an integer second or exactly equal to the DO timestamp. This semantic distinction does not establish a server TTL defect or prove the outstanding live comparison by itself.
- The driver now parses the login response Date, the target Set-Cookie Expires and Domain/Max-Age presence only transiently. It requires wire Expires to equal the session's whole-second expiry exactly, with no Domain and no Max-Age. Browser-stored expiry must be finite and future and satisfy the adjustment range bounded by actual submission-to-cookie-read timing, allowing only 1 millisecond of representation error. Raw headers, cookie values and credential hashes are not retained; no TTL assertion is removed or replaced by an arbitrary future-expiry fallback.
- The fifth fresh `preflight-expiry-fixed` run was executing with the same validation ledger; no successful preflight is claimed yet. Real model validation remains 0/5, with no ambiguous dispatch. Source-170 formal CI was still being observed. Earlier journal snapshots and original C1–C5 evidence remain unchanged.
